alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low Free T4, indicating inadequate thyroid replacement. She reports often forgetting the levothyroxine tablet. Symptoms include tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes — all consistent with hypothyroidism. The 9 kg weight gain over the past year may be substantially attributable to uncontrolled hypothyroidism rather than DTG. The guideline excerpt notes the DTG–weight gain association may not be causal, instead reflecting comparatively less metabolic toxicity than older ART regimens. Switching DTG for weight gain may be premature without first correcting thyroid function and reassessing weight.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence, increase dose to 75 mcg, and recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks before attributing weight gain to DTG or switching ART.

alerts.title: Dyslipidaemia and hyperglycaemia risk on DTG with BMI 33
alerts.message: Guidelines require checking glucose in patients on DTG with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycaemia (age ≥30, BMI ≥25, family history of DM, hypertension). This patient has age 45 and BMI 33 as risk factors; fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is within normal range, providing reassurance. However, LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, and triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L are all elevated, raising cardiovascular risk compounded by obesity. These lipid abnormalities may relate to uncontrolled hypothyroidism, which is a known secondary cause of dyslipidaemia. Correcting thyroid function may improve the lipid profile. No lipid-lowering therapy or dietary intervention was included in today's plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Reassess lipid panel after thyroid optimisation. Consider dietary counselling and lipid-lowering therapy if dyslipidaemia persists. Monitor fasting glucose annually.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines specify that patients on DTG-based first-line ART with VL <50 copies/mL for more than 1 year and reliable adherence can reduce VL monitoring to 12 monthly. This patient's last VL was <50 copies/mL on 2025-11-10, 106 days before the visit. No prior VL result is documented to confirm sustained suppression for over 1 year. If suppression has been maintained for over 12 months, the next VL is due around November 2026. However, if the 2025-11-10 result was the first or only VL, a follow-up VL at 6 months (around May 2026) is indicated. No VL monitoring plan was documented in today's encounter.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm whether VL has been suppressed for over 1 year. If not yet established, schedule next VL at 6 months per guideline monitoring schedule.
